title: Golay-24 Prime Duality of the W(3,3) Substrate
statement: The substrate primes {5,7,11,13} are exactly the primes appearing in the THREE Goldbach decompositions of the Golay dimension 24. Their complements {19,17,13/11} encode the boundary prime, the exotic centralizer prime, and the self-dual pair respectively.

leech_prime_exclusion.note: 23 does NOT appear in any substrate centralizer |C_M(pA)| for p in {5,7,11,13}. 23 is the Leech prime governing M_24, orthogonal to the W(3,3) substrate.

psl2p_connection.statement: For p in {7,11,13}: v3(|C_M(pA)|) - v3(|PSL(2,p)|) = 2. The Monster's p-local centralizer carries exactly 2 extra powers of 3 beyond PSL(2,p), promoted to a full Heisenberg group Heis(F3) = 3^(1+2) of order 27 = gauge_mult.

sylow3_factorization.statement: For p in {7,11,13}: C_M(pA) = [3^3-part] x [3'-part N_p] where N_p = p^2 x 2^(17-p) x extra(p) is a 3-free group.

centralizer_prime_web.note: Non-substrate primes appearing: 17 (complement of 7), 19 (complement of 5). 23 never appears.

opens: MCCXLVII — Why is the Heisenberg group Heis(F3) = 3^(1+2) the universal 3-local envelope? Connection to McKay's E8/E7/E6 observation and the Leech lattice automorphism group.
